question: What is the primary purpose of using tables in nursing research data presentation?

options.A: To make the research paper longer and more complex
options.B: To organize raw numbers systematically so patterns and values are easily understood
options.C: To replace the need for conducting any statistical analysis
options.D: To hide missing data from reviewers and evaluators

explanation: Tables are used to transform unorganized raw numbers into a clear, systematic format so readers can quickly grasp patterns, trends, and specific values. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T6#GNS217_U4_T6_h1)

question: Why is mastering tabular data presentation important for nursing students in Nigeria?

options.A: It allows them to bypass clinical practice requirements
options.B: It ensures evidence-based findings are communicated accurately to healthcare teams and bodies like the NMCN
options.C: It is only required for international publications outside Africa
options.D: It eliminates the need to write a conclusion in research

explanation: Clear presentation ensures that evidence-based findings are communicated accurately to multidisciplinary teams and regulatory bodies such as the Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T6#GNS217_U4_T6_h1)

question: What is the function of the stub in a statistical table?

options.A: To list the main row headings or categories on the left-hand side
options.B: To provide the source note at the very bottom
options.C: To display the main column headings across the top
options.D: To act as the title of the table

explanation: The stub forms the left-hand column of a table and contains the primary row headings or categories being evaluated. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T6#GNS217_U4_T6_h2)

question: Where are footnotes and source notes typically placed in a statistical table?

options.A: At the top above the title
options.B: In the central body inside the data cells
options.C: At the bottom of the table
options.D: In the boxhead beside the column headings

explanation: Footnotes and source notes are placed at the bottom of the table to explain abbreviations, symbols, or data origins. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T6#GNS217_U4_T6_h2)

question: When should a nurse researcher use a frequency distribution table?

options.A: To examine the relationship between three continuous variables simultaneously
options.B: To show how often each value or category of a single variable occurs
options.C: To compare two unrelated qualitative datasets from different hospitals
options.D: To list raw uncalculated observations without any order

explanation: A frequency distribution table is specifically designed to organize and display how often each value or category of a single variable occurs within a dataset. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T6#GNS217_U4_T6_h3)

question: What is the primary purpose of a contingency table in nursing research?

options.A: To examine the relationship between two or more categorical variables
options.B: To track emergency department inventory and medical supplies
options.C: To list the names and licensing numbers of nursing staff
options.D: To replace narrative literature reviews in a thesis

explanation: Contingency tables, or cross-tabulations, are used to analyze the relationship or association between two or more categorical variables. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T6#GNS217_U4_T6_h3)

question: Why should a researcher avoid overcrowding a single table with too many variables?

options.A: It saves space on the computer screen
options.B: It prevents cognitive overload and keeps the data easy for the reader to understand
options.C: It is forbidden by international copyright laws
options.D: It stops statisticians from running Chi-square tests

explanation: Overcrowding a table with too much data causes cognitive overload, making it difficult for the reader to interpret the findings. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T6#GNS217_U4_T6_h4)

question: How should numbers generally be aligned within the columns of a statistical table?

options.B: Aligned by decimal points or right-aligned for easy comparison
options.C: Left-aligned in all circumstances regardless of data type
options.D: Written diagonally to save horizontal space

explanation: Numbers are usually aligned by decimal points or right-aligned so that readers can easily compare magnitudes and values. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T6#GNS217_U4_T6_h4)

question: What is the first step a nursing student should take when interpreting a new table in a research article?

options.B: Read the title, column headers, and row labels to understand context and units
options.C: Assume the data is biased and skip the table entirely
options.D: Look only at the bottom right corner cell

explanation: Before analyzing numbers, one must examine the title, headers, and labels to grasp the context, scope, and units of measurement of the data. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T6#GNS217_U4_T6_h5)

question: Why is it important to check footnotes when interpreting a table?

options.A: Footnotes contain qualifying information like missing data or small sample sizes that affect interpretation
options.B: Footnotes provide the author's home address and telephone number
options.C: Footnotes are required only for decorative purposes in nursing journals
options.D: Footnotes always contain the primary research hypothesis

explanation: Footnotes provide crucial qualifying details, such as explanations of missing data, abbreviations, or sample limitations, which influence how data is interpreted. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T6#GNS217_U4_T6_h5)

question: What does the pitfall of redundancy involve in data presentation?

options.A: Forgetting to include any numbers in the research paper
options.B: Presenting the exact same data repeatedly in the text, in a table, and in a graph
options.C: Using too many different statistical software packages
options.D: Failing to include a reference list at the end of the study

explanation: Redundancy occurs when researchers unnecessarily repeat the same numerical data across the narrative text, tables, and graphs. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T6#GNS217_U4_T6_h6)

question: Why is failing to cite units of measurement in a clinical table considered dangerous?

options.A: It makes the research paper too short to be published
options.B: It can lead to serious clinical misunderstandings regarding patient lab values and dosages
options.C: It automatically invalidates all statistical software calculations
options.D: It prevents the table from having a proper title

explanation: Omitting units of measurement can cause dangerous clinical misunderstandings regarding patient diagnostic values or treatment parameters. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T6#GNS217_U4_T6_h6)
